newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian nickel down in line with world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian nickel down in line with world trend.

text.p: Nickel prices on Tuesday lost the ground they had gained on Monday, dealers said. Other base metals were quiet in a narrow trading range.
"Ready nickel fell by 400 rupees to 39,500 rupees per quintal on demand resistance at higher levels," a dealer said.
Profit-taking, on reports of a setback in the world market, also dragged prices down. Nickel was up 400 rupees on Monday.

"There was no immediate impact on the metal market following reports of American attack on Iraq," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange. "If the war lasts long, arrivals of imported metal may slide."
